title: Ask an imam a good question
whyMatters: A clear question gets a better answer. If you learn how to put something to an imam or a qualified teacher, you save yourself confusion, you get guidance that fits your actual life, and you can tell when a matter needs looking at properly rather than in passing.

subSteps: Say what happened, what you need to decide, and where you live.
Mention deadlines, family pressure, health problems, or money details if they bear on it.
Leave out private details that do not change the answer.
Say you are a new Muslim and you want the practical next step.
Ask what has to happen now and what can wait.
Ask whether there are differences of opinion you should know about, without needing the full detail.

exactActions.text: Double-check before you act on the big things
subSteps: Marriage, divorce, inheritance, zakat, abuse, medical problems, and anything legal all need careful review.
Do not make a major life decision on the strength of anonymous comments.
Get professional help when the issue is medical, legal, or financial.

timeEstimate: 10 to 20 minutes to prepare a clear question

obstacles.problem: I feel embarrassed asking basic questions
obstacles.solution: Basic questions are exactly what a teacher expects from a beginner. Asking plainly beats sitting in silent confusion.
Ask the teacher which answer applies to your situation and which parts can wait. If you need more than that, take it to a qualified local scholar who knows your context.

tinyVersion: Write down three things: what happened, what you need to decide, and that you are a new Muslim.
unlocksNext: Good questions keep you learning with confidence and keep you from acting on bad advice.

gentleScripts.title: Asking for a beginner answer
gentleScripts.body: I am a new Muslim and I am trying to do this properly without getting overwhelmed. What is the practical next step for my situation, and what can wait?
